name: DecryptedText-TS-TW

frames.best_why: All three lines show at once, two finished and the purple line half-decrypted into readable words.

tagline: Words dissolve into random symbols, then snap back into reading order.
summary: A line of text flickers through random letters and punctuation before resolving character by character into the real sentence. It can start on hover, when scrolled into view, or on a click.
appearance: Three lines of bold text stack down a black stage: a large green heading, a medium blue monospaced line and a smaller purple line. Every character keeps its slot, so during the run each word shows some settled letters and some random glyphs.
behaviour: Hovering the first line makes it scrambles then resolve; the second decrypts once as it scrolls into view; the third toggles between plain text and a scramble on each click. While running, a timer swaps unrevealed characters for random glyphs until the true text is restored.
demo_content: Three prompts: Hover over me to decrypt!, Decrypted on view trigger, Click me to reveal the message.
search_phrases: random characters turning into a sentence
text decrypts when scrolled into view
use_when: A tech or sci-fi page wants a heading to feel encoded and then resolve, without a full typewriter.
avoid_when: Constant glyph swapping hurts readability and is motion-heavy; poor for long body copy or calm pages.
customise: Set text, speed and maxIterations, choose hover, view, in-view-hover or click, pick a start, end or centre reveal, and supply a character pool or reuse only the original letters.
weight_why: One interval re-renders a span per character about every 50ms while running.

a11y.note: The real sentence is exposed to screen readers through sr-only text, but the pointer triggers are not focusable.

issues: The clickable line is a span, so click mode cannot be fired from the keyboard.
polish_why: The effect lands well and colours read clearly; the click line has no focus affordance.
title: Decrypted Text
